title: The Wild Duck cluster
caption: The Wild Duck Cluster, Messier 11, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: M 11, Wild Duck Cluster · constellation Scutum · about 6000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Blue stars gather at the center of this image, surrounded by a scattering of redder ones. The blue stars are the young, hot members of the Wild Duck Cluster, an open cluster also cataloged as Messier 11. The redder stars around them are older, cooler stars lying in the background.

A star's color is a guide to its temperature, with hotter stars shining bluer and cooler ones redder. So the color contrast here helps separate the cluster from the unrelated stars behind it, which simply happen to lie in the same direction.

Open clusters are groups of stars born together from the same cloud of gas and dust, so their members share an age. The Wild Duck Cluster lies about 6000 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Scutum. The picture was taken with the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope's Wide Field Imager at La Silla in Chile.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (35.59 x 25.70 arcminutes) and distance (6000 light years), the frame spans roughly 62 × 45 light-years. Its light set out about 6,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and I filters, from visible light into the near-infrared. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The blue and red star colors reflect real differences in temperature, but the I-band data are near-infrared and invisible to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture combines exposures through B, V and I filters, reaching from visible light into the near-infrared. Together the filters bring out both the hot blue cluster members and the cooler, redder stars that lie far behind them.
alt: A cluster of blue stars at the center, surrounded by redder background stars.
